name: InventoriesComponentClientFacet_OnQueryInventories
summary: The inventories facet's answer to a query. Two committed records, 113 and 40912 body bytes. The reader is explicit and gives the shape: shared head, an OPTIONAL nested RequestContext (typeIndex 5828), a u32, a string, a counted vector of 0xa0-byte inventory elements, then a final string. Each 0xa0 element holds a u32, two strings, and two more optional nested service objects. The record's content is item data - 'Gnew-world|...' strings, 'SkinCollection', 'isCollected', 'ItemPool' - and the big record repeats that pattern 428 times over 40 KB. THIS CARD MODELS NO EMITTABLE FIELDS: the nested RequestContext and the two optional service objects inside each element are Javelin service types with their own buses, and their bodies were NOT decoded. Named only so far as measured.
purpose: Return the contents of one or more inventories: the inventory's own identity, the item ids, and per-item collection state. What the client DOES with it is not measured; the Rust server cannot encode this message until the nested service types are modelled, because a codec that silently drops 60 bytes of a 40 KB body would look like understanding it.

created_when: the client asks the inventories facet to query its inventories, or the server pushes them
lifecycle.if_absent: the client has no inventory contents. The client logged facet-target dispatch failures for this wire family in the lab, so it is not established that the client binds a target for every arrival

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 followed by the wide prefix varint a0 5a, i.e. type index 5792 = 0x16a0. fields[] below use BODY offsets. The two committed records differ only in length: 117 and 40916 record bytes, i.e. 113- and 40912-byte bodies.

evidence.ref: object vtable 0x148200868, resolved by the name-accessor walk (its +0x08 slot is the name accessor: see the sentence that names the string). Message-object slots, using the convention meanings.md established on 2026-10-29 for 0xf37 and 0xda2, where the MARSHAL thunk 0x1414c0730 is `mov rax,[rdx]; jmp [rax+0x60]`: +0x58 = FUN_1435f17f0 is the APPLY handler, which resolves a manager singleton through FUN_1416bd7c0 and copies the value in without ever touching the stream; +0x60 = FUN_1435f18d0 is the WRITER, which serializes the body onto the stream; +0x68 = FUN_1435f1970 is the READER, which deserializes the body off the stream

the writer walk: FUN_1435f18d0 calls FUN_1414dbca0 for the shared two-u64 head, then FUN_141726580 for the whole rest of the body, then unlinks the temporaries. FUN_1414dbca0 is two FUN_140877280 head-writes, which is the serialize side of the paired head primitive, so FUN_1435f18d0 is the writer and the body after offset 0x10 is defined by FUN_141726580 alone

FUN_141726580, in wire order: FUN_1415a4920 on object +0x20 (the optional RequestContext); a u32 BE from object +0x18 (FUN_140876e70); a string from object +0x20 (FUN_140876f20); a prefix-varint count (FUN_140877b10) then that many ELEMENTS of stride 0xa0 written by FUN_1415a3ba0 over object +0x10; then a final string from object +0x68. Every primitive named here is a stream WRITE, so this is the serialize order

FUN_1415a3ba0 (one 0xa0 element, iterating an inner vector of stride 0x90 from +0x10): a u32 BE (FUN_140876e70) then TWO strings (FUN_140876f20 at +0x20 and +0x48) then TWO optional nested service objects (FUN_1415a2c70 at +0x70 and +0x80), each a presence byte followed, when 1, by a nested type index, 16 raw bytes and that object's own body

what stays NOT DECODED: the RequestContext body and the two optional service bodies inside each element. They are Javelin service types with their own buses, not plain record codecs; the record functions at 0x1416f9540 and 0x1416f8740 both turn out to be per-type registration lambdas, and the object vtable at 0x148044a90 does not carry a plain writer/reader pair. Resolving them needs either a live unmarshal or their own type records walked one by one

FUN_1415a4920 (optional nested record): one presence byte through the stream raw slot +0x40; when it is 1, FUN_1461684f0 writes the nested type and then the object's own vtable +0x60 writes its body. FUN_1461684f0 writes a prefix-varint type index and then 16 raw bytes. Measured type index: 5828 (0x16c4), which re message-names resolves to RequestContext in trait Javelin::InventoryService - consistent with this being an inventory query

the nested type writer FUN_1461684f0 was decoded in full: a prefix-varint type index written through FUN_140877b10, and when that index is 0 it instead writes one more prefix varint 0 followed by a 16-byte raw run. So a present nested object is a type index plus a 16-byte identity

re message-names 0x16c4 -> 'RequestContext', trait Javelin::InventoryService, which the atlas's aoi-trait-registry.json lists alongside RequestAware and TransactionContext. That the measured nested type index resolves to an inventory-service type is a second signal for reading this message as an inventory query answer

records 0x28_T0x16a0_R.bin (117 bytes) and 0x29_T0x16a0_R.bin (40916 bytes) at seqs 0x28 and 0x29, both with body head 69ceaf9f28443d0d bf85314bbc4a951a. The 40912-byte body holds 428 'isCollected', 237 'SkinCollection' and 857 'Gnew-world|' runs - in that prefix the 'G' is the length byte of a 'new-world|...' string - so entries read like '<item id><...>SkinCollection<...>isCollected'. The 113-byte body holds 'ItemPool' with its length byte 8 at body offset 78, i.e. the string starts at 79
